why:
rcl's options-taking publisher constructor, and the one rcl name in this family we do not define. The CAPABILITY is present under our own spelling: `rclc_publisher_init_with_options(pub, node, type_support, topic, qos, options)` (`nros_generated.h`), and rclc's default form ships under rclc's exact name as `rclc_publisher_init_default`. Ours says `_with_options` where rcl says bare `_init` because rcl has no second constructor to distinguish it from -- its `_init` IS the options-taking form -- while our surface spells the pair `_init_default` / `_init_with_options` across all five entities, so a reader who has seen one has seen them all. See `c:publisher_init_with_options` for the ours-only half and `c:publisher_get_options` for the readback rcl also has and we decline.

An over-long topic creates the entity on a DIFFERENT key and returns `RCL_RET_OK`: silently wrong, no diagnostic at any warning level.
